text:
maria: quick sync from canary this morning. saw duplicated ephemeral chunks when a client reconnect + router hedged to two upstreams. charging doubled for the overlapped window. raising for design tradeoffs.
eli: saw traces — hedged request race + downstream consumer accepted both partials. upstream replicas didn't have a shared resume id namespace.
jon: ugh. is this the same root cause as previous resume-token collision? or different because of hedging?
eli: different vector: when router hedged, both upstreams returned partial frames for the same logical session id. client reconnect presented token that matched both replicas (they issue tokens independently). router accepted whichever response came first then later accepted the other, both advanced billing.
tanya: we have three rough fixes:
  1) global resume-coordination: central session-service issues canonical resume-ids and serializes claims.
  2) hedging-aware dedupe: router maintains in-flight resume-set per client and drops concurrent emissions with same resume-id within a sliding window.
  3) move billing claim to the edge as an idempotent first-class operation (claim RPC returns canonical owner).
sam: cost/latency tradeoffs: (1) adds cross-pop roundtrip on session start/claim -> increases p95; (2) increases memory and is best-effort (race windows); (3) moves complexity into billing side but keeps edge fast if billing is local.
maria: important: we must avoid client-visible stalls on resume. can we make a hybrid: optimistic fast-path + async canonicalization? e.g., accept first partial and emit provisional billing event; canonical claim happens eventually and emits a final settled event; if dupes detected -> emit compensating adjustment.
jon: compensations are a pain for customers. but we can expose "provisional" cost in usage UI until final settlement. enterprise tenants could opt into strict-mode which blocks resume until claim confirmed.
eli: also consider a small change to token contents: include `issued_by` and monotonic `origin_seq` so routers can detect tokens coming from same replica vs different. Example: `Resume: v3|rid=uuid|iss=zone-3|seq=34|crc=abcd`. If `iss` differs across partials -> router treats as potential duplicate and enters dedupe path.
re: sorry reza: i'm +1 on origin metadata. downside: requires sync across model-serving infra to include it in tokens.
tanya: hedging interplay: when router proxies to multiple upstreams we should suppress duplicate downstream writes by tracking `resume_write_bitmap` keyed by (client, resume-id) for short TTL (e.g., 10s). cheap in most cases but pathological tenants with many reconnects might blow memory. we can bound by per-tenant token cache size.
sam: do we have existing per-tenant eviction logic? if not, ops will need knobs.
kai: telemetry needs: `resume.hedged_dupes`, `billing.provisional_events`, `session.claim_latency`, and trace tag `resume.iss_origin`. also tag hedged=true/false.
maria: operational plan: prototype hedging-aware dedupe at router + include `iss` in token from upstream. fall back: if cache miss, we call `POST /session/claim` but non-blocking. if claim returns conflict -> mark provisional as duplicate and schedule compensation.
eli: can we implement the claim RPC as idempotent with quick 50ms in-memory fast path, and longer durable path behind it? That would minimize blocking on common path.
jon: billing teams: we need an SLA on claim RPC for enterprise strict-mode. i'll coordinate.
tanya: we also need clear error signals to clients: `x-resume-status: provisional|final|rejected`. helps clients show accurate progress.
maria: good call. UX layer should avoid double-rendering tokens too.
reza: i can hack a PoC for router dedupe this week. i'll mock token `iss` and implement a small in-memory TTL-set per client.
sam: i'll draft config toggles: `resume.strict_claim=true/false`, `resume.dedupe_ttl_seconds`, `resume.per_tenant_cache_limit`.
kai: i'll add the metrics + dashboards. suggest alert `resume.hedged_dupes_rate > 0.05%` for canary.
ops-bot: scheduled canary guard window: ingress-resume-hedge-v1 -> rollback window 1h starting 2024-02-14T15:00:00Z.
maria: action items: reza -> router PoC dedupe; eli -> token `iss` change in model-serving; sam -> config RFC; jon -> billing claim SLA + idempotent design; kai -> metrics/dashboards; tanya -> memory/eviction cost estimate. sync Friday 09:30 PT.
jon: +1
tanya: +1 :white_check_mark:
maria: thanks all, keep thread small updates here.
